source.text: Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην, ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε.

records.literal_gloss: Pursue the love, be zealous but [for] the spiritual [things], rather but that you may prophesy.

en.L: Pursue love, and be zealous for the spiritual [gifts], but especially that you may prophesy.
en.B: Strive for love, and set your hearts on spiritual gifts, most of all on prophesying.
en.R: Above everything else, work hard at loving others. And try hard to receive the gifts that the Spirit gives, most of all the gift of prophecy, speaking messages from God.

fr.L: Poursuivez l’amour, et aspirez aux [dons] spirituels, mais surtout à prophétiser.
fr.B: Faites de l’amour votre but, et désirez vivement les dons spirituels, surtout celui de prophétiser.
fr.R: Plus que tout, efforcez-vous d’aimer les autres. Et cherchez de tout votre cœur à recevoir les dons que l’Esprit accorde, surtout le don de prophétie : dire des messages qui viennent de Dieu.

decisions.choice: pursue love: make love the goal, and go after it with effort
decisions.reason: Διώκετε is the verb for running after something, pursuing it (Romans 14:19; Philippians 3:12, 14). It joins chapter 13 to chapter 14: love is the aim, and the gifts are to be sought within it.

decisions.choice: the spiritual things: the gifts the Spirit gives
decisions.reason: τὰ πνευματικά is the neuter plural of the adjective used in 12:1. Here it is what the Corinthians are to be zealous for, as the greater gifts are in 12:31, so the gifts are meant.

decisions.choice: especially that you may prophesy: of all the gifts, prophecy is the one to seek most
alternatives: instead of seeking the gifts, seek to prophesy
decisions.reason: μᾶλλον δὲ marks what is preferred. Paul is not setting prophecy against the other gifts, which he has just told them to seek, but ranking it first; verses 2-5 give the reason.

decisions.choice: be zealous for: seek eagerly, set one's heart on
decisions.reason: As in 12:31, where the same verb ζηλοῦτε is used for the greater gifts; it returns in 14:39. It is a good eagerness here, not rivalry.

decisions.choice: set your hearts on (B); try hard to receive (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 12:31 and 14:39, so that readers can see Paul take up the command again.

decisions.choice: the spiritual [gifts] (L); spiritual gifts (B); the gifts that the Spirit gives (R)
decisions.reason: As in 12:1, the levels supply 'gifts' (m2).

decisions.choice: speaking messages from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what prophecy is, as at 11:4, since many readers think only of predicting the future.

decisions.choice: aspirez à (L); désirez vivement (B); cherchez de tout votre cœur à (R), the same words in 14:39
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek eagerly and set one's heart on something (m4). "Soyez zélés" is stiff in modern French; the same French returns in 14:39, where Paul takes up the command again, as the English keeps its words.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ ἀλλὰ θεῷ, οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀκούει, πνεύματι δὲ λαλεῖ μυστήρια·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] for speaking in a tongue not to people speaks but to God; no one for hears, in spirit but he speaks mysteries;

en.L: For the one speaking in a tongue speaks not to people but to God, for no one understands; but in [the] Spirit [the speaker] utters mysteries.
en.B: Someone who speaks in a tongue is speaking not to people but to God. No one understands what is said; in the Spirit, the speaker is uttering mysteries.
en.R: When people speak in tongues, they are not speaking to other people. They are speaking to God. No one else can understand them. The Spirit is helping them speak, but what they say is a mystery to everyone else.

fr.L: Car celui qui parle en langue ne parle pas {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}} mais à Dieu, car personne ne comprend ; mais dans l’Esprit [celui qui parle] dit des mystères.
fr.B: Celui qui parle en langue ne s’adresse pas {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}}, mais à Dieu. Personne ne comprend ce qu’il dit : dans l’Esprit, il prononce des mystères.
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un parle en langues, il ne parle pas aux autres. Il parle à Dieu. Personne d’autre ne peut le comprendre. L’Esprit l’aide à parler, mais ce qu’il dit reste un mystère pour tous les autres.

decisions.choice: speaks to God: a tongue is addressed to God, in prayer or praise
alternatives: a tongue is a message from God to people
decisions.reason: Verses 14-17 speak of praying, singing and giving thanks in a tongue: the speech goes up to God. That is why it does not build up others unless it is interpreted (verse 5).

decisions.choice: hears: understands
decisions.reason: Those present hear the sound; ἀκούει means that no one grasps what is said, as the same verb is used in the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 11:7, where the builders of Babel can no longer understand one another's speech.

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: the Holy Spirit gives the speech
alternatives: in his spirit: with the speaker's own spirit rather than the mind (verse 14)
decisions.reason: πνεύματι has neither an article nor 'my', so it could mean either. The Spirit is the one who gives tongues (12:10-11), which favors the Holy Spirit. Verse 14 ('my spirit prays') speaks of the speaker's own spirit, which favors the other reading. The two are close: in a tongue the speaker's spirit is moved by God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: mysteries: things hidden from the hearers, because no one understands them
alternatives: God's plan, once hidden and now made known, as in 2:7 and 15:51
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Paul μυστήρια usually names God's purpose now revealed. Here the point is that the words stay hidden from those who hear them.

decisions.choice: mysteries (L, B); a mystery to everyone else (R)
decisions.reason: The key term 'mystery' is kept at every level, with its sense here given in m4. Readable says to whom it is a mystery.

decisions.choice: in [the] Spirit [the speaker] utters
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the article and a subject, which the Greek verb leaves unexpressed.

decisions.choice: The Spirit is helping them speak
decisions.reason: Readable says what 'in the Spirit' means, following m3. Since m3 is uncertain, this is marked for reviewers.

decisions.choice: {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}} (L, B); aux autres (R); the same in 14:3
decisions.reason: The English "people" needs no span, but French has to choose a noun for the Greek word for human beings, men and women. The inclusive default says it plainly, with the traditional "aux hommes" as the alternative; Readable says "aux autres", which needs neither.

source.text: ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ οἰκοδομὴν καὶ παράκλησιν καὶ παραμυθίαν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] but prophesying to people speaks building up and encouragement and comfort.

en.L: But the one prophesying speaks to people [for] building up and encouragement and comfort.
en.B: But someone who prophesies speaks to people, and the words build them up, encourage them and comfort them.
en.R: But people who prophesy speak to others. What they say helps others grow stronger, gives them courage, and comforts them.

fr.L: Mais celui qui prophétise parle {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}} [pour l’]édification, l’encouragement et le réconfort.
fr.B: Mais celui qui prophétise parle {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}}, et ses paroles les édifient, les encouragent et les réconfortent.
fr.R: Mais quand quelqu’un prophétise, il parle aux autres. Ce qu’il dit les aide à devenir plus forts, leur donne du courage et les console.

decisions.choice: building up: making the church grow strong, like a building rising on its foundation
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομὴν is the act of building. Paul pictures the church as God's building (3:9-10) and speaks of love building up (8:1; 10:23). The word runs through this chapter (verses 3-5, 12, 17, 26) as the test of every gift.

decisions.choice: encouragement and comfort: urging on, and consoling those who are downcast
decisions.reason: παράκλησιν can mean comfort, appeal or encouragement, and it is the word for comfort in 2 Corinthians 1:3-7. Here it stands beside παραμυθίαν, consolation for those who grieve or lose heart (as in Philippians 2:1), so it has its other sense, encouragement.

decisions.choice: to people: unlike a tongue, prophecy is understood by those who hear it
decisions.reason: The contrast with verse 2 is exact: the one speaks to God, the other to people.

decisions.choice: building up (L); build them up (B); helps others grow stronger (R)
decisions.reason: 'Build up' keeps Paul's picture of a building, as in 8:1, 10:23 and 2 Corinthians 10:8; 'edification' is now church language. Readable says 'grow stronger' throughout the chapter, as 8:1 says 'makes others strong'.

decisions.choice: [for] building up
decisions.reason: The Greek makes the three nouns the object of 'speaks'; Literal supplies 'for' to show that they name what the speech does.

decisions.choice: l’édification, édifier (L, B); aider à devenir plus fort (R), throughout the chapter
decisions.reason: "Édifier" is built on "édifice" and so keeps Paul's picture of a building going up, which the English "build up" keeps; "construire" said of people sounds odd in French. Readable says plainly what is meant, as the English "grow stronger" does.

source.text: ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ ἑαυτὸν οἰκοδομεῖ· ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] speaking in a tongue himself builds up; the [one] but prophesying [the] church builds up.

en.L: The one speaking in a tongue builds up {{gender:themselves|himself}}, but the one prophesying builds up [the] church.
en.B: Those who speak in a tongue build up themselves, but those who prophesy build up the church.
en.R: People who speak in tongues help only themselves grow stronger. But people who prophesy help the whole church grow stronger.

fr.L: Celui qui parle en langue s’édifie lui-même, mais celui qui prophétise édifie l’église.
fr.B: Ceux qui parlent en langue s’édifient eux-mêmes, mais ceux qui prophétisent édifient l’église.
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un parle en langues, il est le seul à devenir plus fort. Mais quand quelqu’un prophétise, il aide toute l’église à devenir plus forte.

decisions.choice: builds up himself: a real benefit, but for the speaker alone
alternatives: a rebuke of a self-centered use of the gift
decisions.reason: Paul does not say that being built up oneself is wrong: he goes on to wish that all spoke in tongues (verse 5) and thanks God for his own gift (verse 18). But the gifts are given for the good of all (12:7), so in the gathering a gift that helps only its user is the lesser.

decisions.choice: church: the believers as they gather together
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίαν has no article: the assembly of believers when they meet. Throughout the chapter Paul has the gathering in view (verses 19, 23, 28).

decisions.choice: Those who speak ... those who prophesy (B); People who ... (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plurals, since men and women alike are meant; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

decisions.choice: only themselves; the whole church
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the contrast between one person and everyone (m1).

decisions.choice: "celui qui ... lui-même" with no gender span, and the same for the generic "il", "lui", "son" throughout the chapter
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:themselves|himself}}, but in French "celui qui" and "quelqu’un" already mean anyone, man or woman, and the pronouns that refer back to them are ordinary generic French (style guide 7).

decisions.choice: l’église, lowercase, throughout the chapter
decisions.reason: Here the church is the believers as they gather (m2), one congregation, so French writes it without the capital kept for the whole body of believers.

source.text: θέλω δὲ πάντας ὑμᾶς λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε· μείζων δὲ ὁ προφητεύων ἢ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσαις, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ διερμηνεύῃ, ἵνα ἡ ἐκκλησία οἰκοδομὴν λάβῃ.

records.literal_gloss: I want now all you to speak in tongues, rather but that you may prophesy; greater and the [one] prophesying than the [one] speaking in tongues, except if not he interprets, so that the church building up may receive.

en.L: Now I want all of you to speak in tongues, but rather that you may prophesy; and the one prophesying [is] greater than the one speaking in tongues, unless [the speaker] interprets, so that the church may receive building up.
en.B: I would be glad for all of you to speak in tongues, but gladder still for you to prophesy. Those who prophesy are greater than those who speak in tongues, unless they also interpret, so that the church receives something that builds it up.
en.R: I would like every one of you to speak in tongues, but I would much rather have you prophesy. Prophesying is more important than speaking in tongues, unless the speakers also interpret what they say. Then the whole church can grow stronger.

fr.L: Or je veux que vous parliez tous en langues, mais plutôt que vous prophétisiez ; et celui qui prophétise [est] plus grand que celui qui parle en langues, à moins que [celui qui parle] n’interprète, afin que l’église reçoive de l’édification.
fr.B: Je serais heureux que vous parliez tous en langues, mais plus heureux encore que vous prophétisiez. Celui qui prophétise est plus grand que celui qui parle en langues, à moins que celui-ci n’interprète aussi, pour que l’église en reçoive quelque chose qui l’édifie.
fr.R: J’aimerais que chacun de vous parle en langues, mais je préférerais de beaucoup que vous prophétisiez. Prophétiser est plus important que parler en langues, sauf si celui qui parle en langues interprète aussi ce qu’il dit. Alors toute l’église peut devenir plus forte.

decisions.choice: I want all of you to speak in tongues: a real wish, though prophecy is the greater one
alternatives: a concession: 'I grant that you may all speak in tongues'
decisions.reason: Paul values the gift (verses 18, 39) and does not forbid it. But μᾶλλον δὲ ('but rather') sets the greater wish beside the lesser one, as in verse 1. The wish recalls Moses' wish that all God's people were prophets (Numbers 11:29).

decisions.choice: greater: of more use to the church
decisions.reason: The last clause gives the measure: the church is built up. μείζων takes up 'the greater gifts' of 12:31.

decisions.choice: unless he interprets: the one who spoke in the tongue also interprets it
decisions.reason: διερμηνεύῃ has no stated subject. The nearest person is the one speaking in tongues, and verse 13 tells such a person to pray to interpret; verse 27 allows another to do it. Either way the condition is that the tongue is understood.

decisions.choice: I would be glad ... but gladder still
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the two wishes as lesser and greater (m1).

decisions.choice: [the speaker] (L); the speakers also interpret what they say (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Readable name the subject chosen in m3; Balanced says 'they also interpret'.

source.text: Νῦν δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἐὰν ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς γλώσσαις λαλῶν, τί ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσω, ἐὰν μὴ ὑμῖν λαλήσω ἢ ἐν ἀποκαλύψει ἢ ἐν γνώσει ἢ ἐν προφητείᾳ ἢ ἐν διδαχῇ;

records.literal_gloss: Now but, brothers, if I come to you in tongues speaking, what you will I benefit, if not to you I speak either in revelation or in knowledge or in prophecy or in teaching?

en.L: But now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you, unless I speak to you either in revelation or in knowledge or in prophecy or in teaching?
en.B: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, suppose I come to you speaking in tongues. What use will I be to you, unless what I say to you brings a revelation, or knowledge, or prophecy, or teaching?
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, suppose I came to visit you and spoke only in tongues. That would not help you at all. To help you, I would need to bring you a revelation from God, or knowledge, or prophecy, or teaching.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, si je viens vers vous parlant en langues, à quoi vous serai-je utile, si je ne vous parle pas soit par révélation, soit par connaissance, soit par prophétie, soit par enseignement ?
fr.B: Alors, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, supposons que je vienne chez vous en parlant en langues. À quoi vous servirais-je, si ce que je vous dis ne vous apporte pas une révélation, une connaissance, une prophétie ou un enseignement ?
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, imaginez que je vienne vous voir et que je parle seulement en langues. Cela ne vous aiderait pas du tout. Pour vous aider, je devrais vous apporter une révélation de Dieu, ou une connaissance, ou une prophétie, ou un enseignement.

decisions.choice: but now: as things are, to come to the point
decisions.reason: Νῦν here draws a conclusion, as in 12:18 and 12:20; it is not about time. Paul now applies verses 1-5 to himself.

decisions.choice: if I come: an example Paul imagines, not a planned visit
decisions.reason: Paul makes himself the test case: even an apostle speaking in tongues would do the church no good.

decisions.choice: revelation, knowledge, prophecy, teaching: kinds of speech the church can understand
alternatives: two pairs: revelation given through prophecy, and knowledge given through teaching
decisions.reason: Paul names four kinds of understandable speech. Some take them as two pairs, an inner gift and the speech that brings it out, but the Greek simply lists them with 'or'. Revelation and teaching come back in the list of verse 26; knowledge and prophecy are gifts named in 12:8-10.

decisions.choice: That would not help you at all.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: a revelation from God
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the revelation.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers, as elsewhere in the letter
decisions.reason: As in English, the church is addressed as men and women together; "frères" stays available as the traditional form.

source.text: ὅμως τὰ ἄψυχα φωνὴν διδόντα, εἴτε αὐλὸς εἴτε κιθάρα, ἐὰν διαστολὴν τοῖς φθόγγοις μὴ δῷ, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ αὐλούμενον ἢ τὸ κιθαριζόμενον;

records.literal_gloss: Likewise the lifeless [things] a sound giving, whether flute or harp, if a distinction to the notes not they give, how will be known the being piped or the being harped?

en.L: Likewise lifeless [things] that give a sound, whether flute or harp: if they do not give a distinction in the notes, how will what is piped or what is harped be known?
en.B: Think of instruments, lifeless as they are, that give out a sound, like the flute or the harp. If their notes are not distinct, how can anyone tell what is being played on the flute or the harp?
en.R: Musical instruments like the flute and the harp are not alive, but they make sounds. If each note does not sound clear and different, no one can tell what tune is being played.

fr.L: De même, les [choses] sans vie qui rendent un son, soit flûte, soit harpe : si elles ne donnent pas de distinction aux notes, comment connaîtra-t-on ce qui est joué sur la flûte ou ce qui est joué sur la harpe ?
fr.B: Pensez aux instruments, sans vie pourtant, qui produisent un son, comme la flûte ou la harpe. Si leurs notes ne sont pas distinctes, comment reconnaîtra-t-on ce qui est joué sur la flûte ou sur la harpe ?
fr.R: Les instruments de musique comme la flûte et la harpe ne sont pas vivants, mais ils produisent des sons. Si chaque note n’est pas claire et différente des autres, personne ne peut reconnaître l’air qu’on joue.

decisions.choice: likewise: in the same way, introducing a comparison
decisions.reason: ὅμως usually means 'nevertheless', but here, as in Galatians 3:15, it introduces a comparison, and some read it with a different accent as 'likewise'. Either way the instruments illustrate the point.

decisions.choice: flute and harp: a wind instrument and a stringed instrument of the Greek world
decisions.reason: The αὐλὸς was a reed pipe, often played in pairs, heard at feasts, weddings, funerals and in the worship of the gods. The κιθάρα was a lyre with a wooden sound box, plucked with the fingers or a pick. Paul names the most common instruments.

decisions.choice: a distinction in the notes: notes that differ from one another, so that a tune can be heard
decisions.reason: διαστολὴν is a difference or separation; φθόγγοις are musical sounds. A tune is heard only when the notes are distinct.

decisions.choice: flute, harp
decisions.reason: 'Flute' and 'harp' are the nearest instruments familiar to modern readers; m2 describes the actual instruments.

decisions.choice: no one can tell what tune is being played
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer to the question.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἄδηλον φωνὴν σάλπιγξ δῷ, τίς παρασκευάσεται εἰς πόλεμον;

records.literal_gloss: Also for if an unclear sound a trumpet gives, who will prepare himself for battle?

en.L: For indeed, if a trumpet gives an unclear sound, who will prepare for battle?
en.B: And if a trumpet sounds a signal no one can make out, who will prepare to fight?
en.R: In an army, a trumpet tells the soldiers to get ready for battle. But if the trumpet does not play a clear call, no one will know it is time to get ready.

fr.L: Et en effet, si une trompette rend un son indistinct, qui se préparera au combat ?
fr.B: Et si la trompette donne un signal que personne ne peut reconnaître, qui se préparera à combattre ?
fr.R: Dans une armée, la trompette annonce aux soldats qu’ils doivent se préparer au combat. Mais si la trompette ne joue pas un appel clair, personne ne saura que c’est le moment de se préparer.

decisions.choice: trumpet: an instrument used to give signals in war
decisions.reason: Armies were called to arms and given orders by trumpet calls (Numbers 10:9; Jeremiah 4:19). A call no one can recognize leaves the soldiers unprepared.

decisions.choice: who will prepare?: no one will
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer 'no one'.

decisions.choice: In an army, a trumpet tells the soldiers to get ready for battle.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a trumpet call was for (m1) and gives the answer to the question (m2).

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς διὰ τῆς γλώσσης ἐὰν μὴ εὔσημον λόγον δῶτε, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ λαλούμενον;

records.literal_gloss: So also you through the tongue if not a clear word you give, how will be known the being spoken?

en.L: So also you: unless you give a clear word through the tongue, how will what is spoken be known?
en.B: So with you: if your tongue does not produce speech that makes sense, how will what you say be understood?
en.R: It is like that for you too. When you speak, others need words they can understand. Otherwise they cannot tell what you mean.

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi : si par la langue vous ne donnez pas une parole claire, comment connaîtra-t-on ce qui est dit ?
fr.B: Il en va de même pour vous : si votre langue ne produit pas des paroles qui ont un sens, comment comprendra-t-on ce que vous dites ?
fr.R: C’est la même chose pour vous. Quand vous parlez, les autres ont besoin de mots qu’ils comprennent. Sinon, ils ne peuvent pas savoir ce que vous voulez dire.

decisions.choice: through the tongue: with the tongue as the organ of speech
decisions.reason: τῆς γλώσσης has the article, and 'through the tongue' fits the tongue in the mouth, as the instruments of verses 7-8 make sound. Paul may be playing on the word, which also names the gift; the point is the same either way: speech must be understood.

decisions.choice: clear: easily recognized, with a plain meaning
decisions.reason: εὔσημον means well marked, distinct, the opposite of the trumpet's unclear sound in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Otherwise they cannot tell what you mean.
alternatives: how will what is spoken be known?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into statements.

source.text: ἔσεσθε γὰρ εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες.

records.literal_gloss: You will be for into air speaking.

en.L: For you will be speaking into [the] air.
en.B: You will be speaking to empty air.
en.R: Your words will be wasted, like talking to the wind.

fr.L: Car vous parlerez dans l’air.
fr.B: Vous parlerez dans le vide.
fr.R: Vos paroles seront perdues, comme si vous parliez au vent.

decisions.choice: speaking into the air: talking to no purpose
decisions.reason: Like 'beating the air' (9:26), the phrase describes effort that reaches no one.

decisions.choice: like talking to the wind
decisions.reason: Readable uses a familiar picture for words that reach no one.

decisions.choice: dans l’air (L); dans le vide (B)
decisions.reason: French "parler en l’air" means to talk thoughtlessly or make empty promises, not to speak to no purpose (m1). "Parler dans le vide" is the French idiom for words that reach no one; Literal keeps the air.

source.text: τοσαῦτα εἰ τύχοι γένη φωνῶν εἰσιν ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ οὐδὲν ἄφωνον·

records.literal_gloss: So many, if it may happen, kinds of sounds there are in [the] world, and nothing [is] without sound;

en.L: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in [the] world, and none [is] without meaning;
en.B: Who knows how many languages there are in the world? And not one of them is without meaning.
en.R: There are many, many languages in the world, and every one of them means something to the people who speak it.

fr.L: Il y a, peut-être, tant de sortes de langages dans le monde, et aucun [n’est] sans signification ;
fr.B: Qui sait combien il y a de langages dans le monde ? Et aucun n’est dépourvu de sens.
fr.R: Il y a beaucoup, beaucoup de langues dans le monde, et chacune a un sens pour les gens qui la parlent.

decisions.choice: it may be: perhaps, who knows how many
decisions.reason: εἰ τύχοι is an idiom for 'perhaps' or 'as it happens'; here it stresses that the number is great and not known.

decisions.choice: sounds: languages, human speech
decisions.reason: φωνῶν is the word used for the sound of the instruments in verses 7-8. Here the kinds of 'sound' in the world are languages, as verse 11 shows.

decisions.choice: without meaning: a play on words, literally 'soundless'
decisions.reason: ἄφωνον is formed from the same word with a negative. Here it means without meaning: every language communicates to those who know it.

decisions.choice: world: the inhabited world, humankind with its many peoples
decisions.reason: κόσμῳ here is the world of people and their languages, not the created universe or the world opposed to God.

decisions.choice: languages
decisions.reason: Every level says 'languages', since that is the sense here (m2); the gloss keeps 'sounds'.

decisions.choice: langages (L, B); langues (R); the same in 14:11
decisions.reason: French "langue" is also the word for a "tongue" in this chapter, so Literal and Balanced say "langage" for this different Greek word, as the English keeps "languages" apart from "tongues". Readable uses the everyday word.

source.text: ἐὰν οὖν μὴ εἰδῶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς φωνῆς, ἔσομαι τῷ λαλοῦντι βάρβαρος καὶ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν ἐμοὶ βάρβαρος.

records.literal_gloss: If therefore not I know the power of the sound, I will be to the [one] speaking a foreigner and the [one] speaking in me a foreigner.

en.L: So if I do not know the force of the language, I will be a foreigner to the one speaking, and the one speaking [will be] a foreigner to me.
en.B: If I do not understand the language someone speaks, we will be foreigners to each other: I to the speaker, and the speaker to me.
en.R: If I do not understand what someone is saying, we are like strangers from different countries who cannot talk to each other.

fr.L: Si donc je ne connais pas la force du langage, je serai un étranger pour celui qui parle, et celui qui parle [sera] un étranger pour moi.
fr.B: Si je ne comprends pas le langage que parle quelqu’un, nous serons des étrangers l’un pour l’autre : moi pour lui, et lui pour moi.
fr.R: Si je ne comprends pas ce que quelqu’un dit, nous sommes comme des gens de pays différents qui ne peuvent pas se parler.

decisions.choice: force: meaning
decisions.reason: δύναμιν usually means power; of a word or a language it means what it conveys, its meaning.

decisions.choice: foreigner: someone whose language one cannot understand
decisions.reason: βάρβαρος first named a person whose speech sounded to Greeks like meaningless 'bar-bar'. It was used of non-Greeks (Romans 1:14; Colossians 3:11; Acts 28:2), without necessarily meaning savage. Here each of two people is a foreigner to the other, because neither understands.

decisions.choice: in me: in my view, to me
decisions.reason: ἐν ἐμοὶ means 'in my judgment', 'as far as I am concerned'.

decisions.choice: foreigner (L, B); strangers from different countries (R)
decisions.reason: 'Barbarian' now suggests someone uncivilized, which is not the point (m2).

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ἐπεὶ ζηλωταί ἐστε πνευμάτων, πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ζητεῖτε ἵνα περισσεύητε.

records.literal_gloss: So also you, since zealots you are of spirits, for the building up of the church seek that you may abound.

en.L: So also you, since you are zealous for spirits, seek to abound for the building up of the church.
en.B: It is the same with you. Since you are so eager for the workings of the Spirit, aim to have them in abundance for the building up of the church.
en.R: That is true for you too. You really want the Spirit to work through you. So try hard to have plenty of the gifts that help the church grow stronger.

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi, puisque vous êtes zélés pour les esprits, cherchez à abonder pour l’édification de l’église.
fr.B: Il en va de même pour vous. Puisque vous êtes si avides de ce que l’Esprit accomplit, cherchez à en être riches pour l’édification de l’église.
fr.R: C’est vrai pour vous aussi. Vous désirez vraiment que l’Esprit agisse par vous. Alors efforcez-vous d’avoir en abondance les dons qui aident l’église à devenir plus forte.

decisions.choice: spirits: the ways the one Spirit is at work in the gifts
alternatives: spirits or spiritual powers in general
spiritual gifts, the same as in verse 1
decisions.reason: πνευμάτων is the plural of 'spirit'. Paul probably means the many ways the one Spirit shows his presence in the gifts (12:7, 'the manifestation of the Spirit'); compare 'the spirits of prophets' in verse 32. Some take it as a looser way of saying 'spiritual gifts'.

decisions.choice: seek to abound for the building up of the church: the church's growth is to be the goal of their eagerness
alternatives: seek to abound in the gifts that build up the church
decisions.reason: πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας stands first for emphasis. Paul does not discourage their eagerness; he gives it a goal.

decisions.choice: zealots: eager, keen
decisions.reason: ζηλωταί is the noun related to 'be zealous' in verses 1 and 39; it describes the Corinthians' strong desire, which Paul does not condemn.

decisions.choice: the workings of the Spirit (B); the Spirit to work through you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what 'spirits' means here (m1); Literal keeps 'spirits'.

source.text: Διὸ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ προσευχέσθω ἵνα διερμηνεύῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore the [one] speaking in a tongue let him pray that he may interpret.

en.L: Therefore let the one speaking in a tongue pray that {{gender:they|he}} may interpret.
en.B: For that reason, anyone who speaks in a tongue should ask God for the power to interpret it as well.
en.R: So people who speak in tongues should pray that God will also help them interpret what they say.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, que celui qui parle en langue prie afin d’interpréter.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi celui qui parle en langue doit demander à Dieu de pouvoir aussi l’interpréter.
fr.R: Donc, celui qui parle en langues doit prier pour que Dieu l’aide aussi à interpréter ce qu’il dit.

decisions.choice: pray that he may interpret: ask God for the gift of interpretation
alternatives: pray in the tongue in such a way that it can then be interpreted
decisions.reason: ἵνα can give the content of the prayer or its purpose. Since interpretation is a gift of the Spirit (12:10), the speaker is told to ask for it.

decisions.choice: therefore: because only a tongue that is interpreted builds up the church
decisions.reason: Διὸ draws the conclusion of verses 5 and 12.

decisions.choice: ask God for the power to interpret it as well (B); pray that God will also help them interpret (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say to whom the prayer is made and what is asked (m1).

source.text: ἐὰν γὰρ προσεύχωμαι γλώσσῃ, τὸ πνεῦμά μου προσεύχεται, ὁ δὲ νοῦς μου ἄκαρπός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: If for I pray in a tongue, the spirit of me prays, the but mind of me unfruitful is.

en.L: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is fruitless.
en.B: When I pray in a tongue, it is my spirit that prays, while my mind bears no fruit.
en.R: When I pray in tongues, my spirit is praying, but my mind is not doing anything useful.

fr.L: Car si je prie en langue, mon esprit prie, mais mon intelligence est sans fruit.
fr.B: Quand je prie en langue, c’est mon esprit qui prie, mais mon intelligence ne porte pas de fruit.
fr.R: Quand je prie en langues, mon esprit prie, mais mon intelligence ne fait rien d’utile.

decisions.choice: my spirit: the speaker's own inner self, moved by God's Spirit
alternatives: the Holy Spirit given to me, praying through me
decisions.reason: With 'my', τὸ πνεῦμά μου most naturally means Paul's own spirit, the part of a person that relates to God (2:11; Romans 8:16), here set against his mind. Some read it as the Holy Spirit at work in Paul, since tongues are a gift of the Spirit (12:10). The two are not far apart: in a tongue the Spirit prays through the human spirit without passing through the mind.

decisions.choice: mind: the power of understanding and thinking
decisions.reason: νοῦς is the mind as it understands and reasons (verse 19; 2:16; Romans 12:2).

decisions.choice: without fruit: producing nothing, neither understanding for the speaker nor benefit for others
decisions.reason: ἄκαρπός means barren, yielding nothing. Paul's mind does not understand the words and so has nothing to give the church; verse 19 sets speaking 'with my mind' against this, so that others are taught.

decisions.choice: bears no fruit (B); not doing anything useful (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture; Readable says plainly what it means (m3).

decisions.choice: l’intelligence, at every level and in 14:15 and 14:19
decisions.reason: "L’esprit" is needed for the other Greek word in the same sentence, and "la pensée" names a thought rather than the power of understanding (m2). "Intelligence" in its older sense of understanding is the clearest French for it.

source.text: τί οὖν ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: What then is it?

en.L: What then is [it]?
en.B: What follows, then?
en.R: So what will I do?

fr.L: Qu’en est-il donc ?
fr.B: Que conclure, alors ?
fr.R: Alors, que vais-je faire ?

decisions.choice: what then is it?: what is the conclusion?
decisions.reason: The short question, used again in verse 26, introduces Paul's conclusion.

decisions.choice: What follows, then? (B); So what will I do? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the question; Readable puts it in terms of what Paul will do, which the next sentence answers.

source.text: προσεύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι, προσεύξομαι δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ· ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι, ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ·

records.literal_gloss: I will pray with the spirit, I will pray but also with the mind; I will sing praise with the spirit, I will sing praise but also with the mind;

en.L: I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray also with the mind; I will sing praise with the spirit, but I will sing praise also with the mind.
en.B: I will pray in the spirit, and I will pray with my mind as well. I will sing praise in the spirit, and I will sing praise with my mind as well.
en.R: I will pray with my spirit, in tongues, and I will also pray with my mind, in words I understand. I will sing with my spirit, in tongues, and I will also sing with my mind, in words I understand.

fr.L: Je prierai avec l’esprit, mais je prierai aussi avec l’intelligence ; je chanterai des louanges avec l’esprit, mais je chanterai des louanges aussi avec l’intelligence.
fr.B: Je prierai en esprit, et je prierai aussi avec mon intelligence. Je chanterai des louanges en esprit, et je chanterai aussi des louanges avec mon intelligence.
fr.R: Je prierai avec mon esprit, en langues, et je prierai aussi avec mon intelligence, avec des mots que je comprends. Je chanterai avec mon esprit, en langues, et je chanterai aussi avec mon intelligence, avec des mots que je comprends.

decisions.choice: with the spirit: with one's own spirit, in a tongue, as in verse 14
decisions.reason: τῷ πνεύματι takes up 'my spirit' of verse 14, and the article points back to it. Praying 'with the spirit' is praying in a tongue; praying 'with the mind' is praying in words one understands. As in verse 14, the human spirit is moved by the Spirit of God.

decisions.choice: sing praise: sing to God
decisions.reason: ψαλῶ is related to the word 'psalm' (verse 26) and means to sing praise to God (Romans 15:9; James 5:13).

decisions.choice: I will: Paul's resolve, set out as a pattern
decisions.reason: The future verbs say what Paul will do. He does not give up praying in tongues, but he joins understanding to it.

decisions.choice: spirit, with a lowercase s
decisions.reason: Lowercase 'spirit' follows the choice in m1, the human spirit; the footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: in tongues; in words I understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what praying with the spirit and with the mind mean (m1).

source.text: ἐπεὶ ἐὰν εὐλογῇς πνεύματι, ὁ ἀναπληρῶν τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἰδιώτου πῶς ἐρεῖ τὸ Ἀμήν ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ;

records.literal_gloss: Otherwise if you bless in spirit, the [one] filling the place of the outsider how will he say the Amen at your thanksgiving?

en.L: Otherwise, if you bless [God] in [the] spirit, how will the one filling the place of the outsider say the "Amen" at your thanksgiving?
en.B: Otherwise, if you bless God in the spirit, how will someone who is in the outsider's place say the "Amen" to your prayer of thanks?
en.R: Suppose you praise God only with your spirit. Someone there who does not understand cannot say "Amen" to agree with your prayer of thanks.

fr.L: Autrement, si tu bénis [Dieu] en esprit, comment celui qui occupe la place du non-initié dira-t-il l’« Amen » à ton action de grâce ?
fr.B: Autrement, si tu bénis Dieu en esprit, comment celui qui se trouve à la place du non-initié pourra-t-il répondre « Amen » à ta prière de remerciement ?
fr.R: Imagine que tu loues Dieu seulement avec ton esprit. Quelqu’un qui est là et qui ne comprend pas ne peut pas dire « Amen » pour montrer qu’il est d’accord avec ta prière de remerciement.

decisions.choice: bless: praise and thank God
decisions.reason: εὐλογῇς, used of people speaking to God, means to praise him and give thanks, as at a meal (10:16). At the end of the sentence the prayer is called a thanksgiving.

decisions.choice: in the spirit: with one's own spirit, in a tongue, as in verses 14-15
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the outsider: someone in the gathering who does not share the gift and cannot understand the tongue, perhaps one not yet fully part of the church
alternatives: an ordinary believer without the gift of tongues or of interpretation
an inquirer, someone interested in the faith but not yet a believer
decisions.reason: ἰδιώτου means a private person, someone without special skill or knowledge (Acts 4:13; 2 Corinthians 11:6). In verses 23-24 the same word stands beside 'unbelievers' but is distinct from them, so it may be someone who attends but has not yet joined the church, or any believer who lacks the gift. Either way the person cannot understand what is said in the tongue.

decisions.choice: filling the place of the outsider: being in the position of one who does not understand
alternatives: sitting in a particular place in the room set aside for outsiders
decisions.reason: ἀναπληρῶν means to fill or occupy. It most likely describes a person's role or situation. Some think of an actual place where visitors sat, but nothing else is known of such seating in the house churches.

decisions.choice: Amen: the word by which hearers agree with a prayer and make it their own
decisions.reason: Ἀμήν is a Hebrew word meaning 'it is true, so be it'. The congregation said it at the end of prayers and blessings (Deuteronomy 27:15-26; Nehemiah 8:6; 2 Corinthians 1:20). No one can say it to a prayer they have not understood.

decisions.choice: outsider
decisions.reason: 'Outsider' says that the person stands outside what is happening, without deciding between the readings in m3.

decisions.choice: only; Someone there who does not understand; to agree with
decisions.reason: Readable names the outsider by the one thing certain about the person, that they do not understand (m3), and says what 'Amen' does (m5).

decisions.choice: prayer of thanks
decisions.reason: 'Thanksgiving' alone may suggest the holiday; the Greek word is a prayer of thanks.

decisions.choice: le non-initié (L, B); quelqu’un qui ne comprend pas (R); the same in 14:23-24
decisions.reason: Like the English "outsider", "non-initié" says that the person stands outside what is happening, without choosing between the readings in m3. "Profane" would suggest someone without religion, and "étranger" is kept for the foreigner of 14:11.

decisions.choice: tu, ton, ta in 14:16-17
decisions.reason: Paul turns here to one imagined speaker; the Greek verbs and pronouns are singular, so French says "tu" (style guide 6), where English "you" does not show the change.

source.text: ἐπειδὴ τί λέγεις οὐκ οἶδεν·

records.literal_gloss: since what you say not he knows;

en.L: since [the outsider] does not know what you are saying.
en.B: That person has no idea what you are saying.
en.R: That person does not know what you are saying.

fr.L: puisque [le non-initié] ne sait pas ce que tu dis.
fr.B: Celui-là ne sait pas du tout ce que tu dis.
fr.R: Il ne sait pas ce que tu dis.

decisions.choice: since: the reason the outsider cannot say the Amen
decisions.reason: ἐπειδὴ gives the reason for the question before.

decisions.choice: [the outsider] (L); That person (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject; the levels name the outsider of the sentence before.

source.text: σὺ μὲν γὰρ καλῶς εὐχαριστεῖς, ἀλλ’ ὁ ἕτερος οὐκ οἰκοδομεῖται.

records.literal_gloss: You indeed for well give thanks, but the other not is built up.

en.L: For you indeed give thanks well, but the other [person] is not built up.
en.B: Your thanksgiving may be fine, but it does nothing to build up the other person.
en.R: Your prayer of thanks may be good, but it does not help the other person grow stronger.

fr.L: Car toi, certes, tu rends bien grâce, mais l’autre n’est pas édifié.
fr.B: Ta prière de remerciement est peut-être belle, mais elle n’édifie en rien l’autre.
fr.R: Ta prière de remerciement est peut-être bonne, mais elle n’aide pas l’autre à devenir plus fort.

decisions.choice: you give thanks well: Paul grants that the prayer itself is good
decisions.reason: μὲν ('indeed') concedes the point before the 'but'. The fault is not in the prayer but in its effect: no one else is helped.

decisions.choice: is built up: is helped to grow, as in verses 3-5
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομεῖται is the verb of verse 4.

decisions.choice: build up (B); grow stronger (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

source.text: εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ, πάντων ὑμῶν μᾶλλον γλώσσαις λαλῶ·

records.literal_gloss: I give thanks to the God, than all of you more in tongues I speak;

en.L: I thank God, I speak in tongues more than you all;
en.B: I am thankful to God that, more than every one of you, I speak in tongues.
en.R: I speak in tongues more than any of you, and I thank God for it.

fr.L: Je rends grâce à Dieu, je parle en langues plus que vous tous ;
fr.B: Je remercie Dieu de ce que je parle en langues plus que vous tous.
fr.R: Je parle en langues plus que n’importe lequel d’entre vous, et j’en remercie Dieu.

decisions.choice: I thank God: the thanks is for the fact that follows
decisions.reason: The Greek sets the two clauses side by side with no 'that'; the second says what Paul thanks God for.

decisions.choice: Paul does not despise tongues
decisions.reason: Paul has the gift in greater measure than the Corinthians who prize it. What he says about its limits in the gathering (verse 19) comes from one who values it.

decisions.choice: more than all of you: more than any of you
alternatives: in more kinds of tongues than you
decisions.reason: μᾶλλον can mean more often or to a greater degree; the comparison is with every one of them.

decisions.choice: that
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses with 'that' (m1).

decisions.choice: the fact first, then the thanks
decisions.reason: Readable states what Paul does before thanking God for it.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ θέλω πέντε λόγους τῷ νοΐ μου λαλῆσαι, ἵνα καὶ ἄλλους κατηχήσω, ἢ μυρίους λόγους ἐν γλώσσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: But in church I want five words with the mind of me to speak, so that also others I may instruct, than ten thousand words in a tongue.

en.L: But in church I would rather speak five words with my mind, so that I may also instruct others, than 10,000 words in a tongue.
en.B: But when the church meets, I would sooner speak five words with my mind, so as to teach others too, than thousands upon thousands of words in a tongue.
en.R: But when the church meets together, I would rather say five words that I understand, so that others can learn from them too, than thousands of words in tongues.

fr.L: Mais dans l’église je préfère dire cinq paroles avec mon intelligence, afin d’instruire aussi les autres, plutôt que dix mille paroles en langue.
fr.B: Mais quand l’église est réunie, j’aime mieux dire cinq mots avec mon intelligence, pour instruire aussi les autres, que des milliers et des milliers de mots en langue.
fr.R: Mais quand l’église se réunit, je préfère dire cinq mots que je comprends, pour que les autres apprennent aussi quelque chose, plutôt que des milliers de mots en langues.

decisions.choice: I want ... than: I would prefer
decisions.reason: θέλω followed by ἢ ('than') expresses a preference.

decisions.choice: in church: in the gathering of believers
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, ἐκκλησίᾳ without the article means the assembly when it meets. The contrast with verse 18 suggests that Paul uses tongues elsewhere, in his own prayer.

decisions.choice: instruct: teach
decisions.reason: κατηχήσω means to teach by word of mouth (Romans 2:18; Galatians 6:6).

decisions.choice: ten thousand: a number too great to count
decisions.reason: As in 4:15, μυρίους is the largest Greek number word and stands for a great many; set beside 'five', it makes the contrast as sharp as possible.

decisions.choice: 10,000 (L); thousands upon thousands (B); thousands (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the number, written in figures as in 4:15; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m4). 'Five' is written as a word.

decisions.choice: five words that I understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what speaking with the mind means, as in verse 15.

decisions.choice: dix mille, in words
decisions.reason: The English writes the figure; French writes round numbers in words in running text (style guide 4). Balanced and Readable give the sense, as in English (m4).

source.text: Ἀδελφοί, μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσίν, ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε, ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶν τέλειοι γίνεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: Brothers, not children be in the thinking, but in the evil be infants, in the but thinking mature be.

en.L: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, do not become children in [your] minds; rather, in wickedness be babies, but in [your] minds become mature.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, do not think like children. Be babies where evil is concerned, but in your understanding be grown up.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, stop thinking like little children. When it comes to doing wrong, be like babies who know nothing about it. But in the way you think, be grown-ups.

fr.L: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, ne devenez pas des enfants dans [vos] pensées ; mais pour la méchanceté, soyez des tout-petits, et dans [vos] pensées, devenez mûrs.
fr.B: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, ne raisonnez pas comme des enfants. Pour le mal, soyez des tout-petits, mais pour le jugement, soyez des adultes.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, arrêtez de penser comme de petits enfants. Pour ce qui est de faire le mal, soyez comme des bébés qui n’y connaissent rien. Mais dans votre façon de penser, soyez des adultes.

decisions.choice: minds: thinking, judgment
decisions.reason: φρεσίν is the mind as it thinks and judges; the word occurs only here in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: children, babies, mature: stages of growing up
decisions.reason: παιδία are young children, νηπιάζετε means to be like an infant, and τέλειοι are those who are grown, the mature (2:6). Paul wants them innocent of evil but adult in judgment, the judgment their love of tongues lacked. Compare 3:1-2 and 13:11.

decisions.choice: wickedness: evil, malice
decisions.reason: κακίᾳ is badness of every kind, including ill will toward others (5:8).

decisions.choice: grown up (B); grown-ups (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words keep the picture of growing up; Literal keeps 'mature', as in 2:6.

source.text: ἐν τῷ νόμῳ γέγραπται ὅτι Ἐν ἑτερογλώσσοις καὶ ἐν χείλεσιν ἑτέρων λαλήσω τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ, καὶ οὐδ’ οὕτως εἰσακούσονταί μου, λέγει κύριος.

records.literal_gloss: In the law it has been written that, By [people of] other tongues and by lips of others I will speak to the people this, and not even thus will they listen to me, says [the] Lord.

en.L: In the law it is written, "By [people of] other tongues and by [the] lips of others I will speak to this people, and not even so will they listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says [the] Lord."
en.B: It is written in the law: "Through those who speak other tongues, and through the lips of strangers, I will speak to this people; and not even then will they heed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says the Lord."
en.R: In the law, God's written word, the Lord says, "I will speak to this people through foreigners who speak other tongues. But they will still not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: Dans la Loi il est écrit : « Par des [gens d’]autres langues et par des lèvres d’étrangers je parlerai à ce peuple, et même ainsi ils ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écouteront pas, dit le Seigneur. »
fr.B: Il est écrit dans la Loi : « C’est par des gens qui parlent d’autres langues, par la bouche d’étrangers, que je parlerai à ce peuple ; et même alors, ils ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écouteront pas, dit le Seigneur. »
fr.R: Dans la Loi, la parole écrite de Dieu, le Seigneur dit : « Je parlerai à ce peuple par des étrangers qui parlent d’autres langues. Mais même alors, ils ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écouteront pas. »

decisions.choice: a quotation of Isaiah 28:11-12
decisions.reason: Paul quotes Isaiah 28:11-12 freely: his wording follows neither the Hebrew nor the Greek Old Testament closely, and he has God speak in the first person ('I will speak'). In Isaiah the LORD warns the people of Jerusalem, who mocked the prophet's plain message, that he will speak to them through the foreign speech of Assyrian invaders, and even then they will not listen. Reviewers should check the wording against both.

decisions.choice: the law: the Scriptures as a whole
decisions.reason: Isaiah is not one of the books of Moses, but νόμῳ could stand for the whole of Scripture (John 10:34, quoting a psalm; Romans 3:10-19, where words from the Psalms and Isaiah are called what 'the law says').

decisions.choice: says the Lord: the God of Israel speaks; the divine name stands behind 'Lord'
decisions.reason: These words are not in Isaiah 28:11-12. Paul adds the formula with which the prophets mark God's own speech, as in Isaiah 1:11 and often. In the Hebrew prophets that formula uses the divine name, the LORD; the Greek Old Testament and Paul have κύριος.

decisions.choice: other tongues, lips of others: foreign languages
decisions.reason: ἑτερογλώσσοις means people of another language. In Isaiah the foreign speech is a sign of judgment on those who would not listen to the plain word; Paul draws on that in verse 22.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: As in 3:20: Paul's Greek has the word for 'Lord', so English writes 'Lord', and m3 notes the divine name behind it.

decisions.choice: God's written word
decisions.reason: Readable explains that 'the law' here means the Scriptures (m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: foreigners who speak other tongues
decisions.reason: Readable keeps 'tongues', the word of this chapter, and says that the speakers are foreigners, as in Isaiah (m4).

source.text: ὥστε αἱ γλῶσσαι εἰς σημεῖόν εἰσιν οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἀπίστοις, ἡ δὲ προφητεία οὐ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἀλλὰ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: So that the tongues for a sign are not to the believing but to the unbelieving, the but prophecy not to the unbelieving but to the believing.

en.L: So then tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe but to unbelievers; but prophecy [is] not to unbelievers but to those who believe.
en.B: So tongues serve as a sign, but the sign is for unbelievers, not for those who believe. Prophecy, on the other hand, is for those who believe, not for unbelievers.
en.R: So speaking in tongues is a sign for people who do not believe, not for believers. But prophecy is for believers, not for people who do not believe.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, les langues sont un signe, non pour ceux qui croient, mais pour les incroyants ; tandis que la prophétie [est] non pour les incroyants, mais pour ceux qui croient.
fr.B: Ainsi, les langues servent de signe, mais ce signe est pour les incroyants, non pour ceux qui croient. La prophétie, elle, est pour ceux qui croient, non pour les incroyants.
fr.R: Donc, parler en langues est un signe pour ceux qui ne croient pas, et non pour les croyants. Mais la prophétie est pour les croyants, et non pour ceux qui ne croient pas.

decisions.choice: so then: a conclusion drawn from the quotation
decisions.reason: ὥστε draws the lesson of Isaiah 28:11-12 (verse 21).

decisions.choice: a sign for unbelievers: a sign of judgment, which leaves them in their unbelief, as the foreign speech did in Isaiah
alternatives: a sign meant to lead unbelievers to faith, as at Pentecost (Acts 2:5-12)
a sign that shows who the unbelievers are, because they cannot understand
Paul quotes a view held in Corinth and corrects it in verses 23-25
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the strange speech of foreigners came on a people who refused to listen, and 'even then they will not listen' (verse 21). Verse 23 bears this out: unbelievers who hear tongues say 'you are raving' and do not come to faith. The sentence is hard, because verses 24-25 show prophecy at work on an unbeliever, which seems to reverse what this verse says of prophecy.

decisions.choice: prophecy is for believers: it serves those who believe; whether it is also called a sign is left open
alternatives: prophecy is a sign for believers, of God's presence among them
decisions.reason: The second half has no verb and does not repeat 'sign'. It may mean simply that prophecy is meant for believers, or that it is a sign for them. Verses 24-25 show that it also reaches an unbeliever who hears it.

decisions.choice: unbelievers: people who do not believe in Christ
decisions.reason: ἀπίστοις means people who do not believe, as in 6:6 and 7:12-15; in verses 23-24 they stand beside outsiders.

decisions.choice: the group each gift is for comes first
alternatives: not for believers but for unbelievers
decisions.reason: Balanced names first the group each gift is for, which makes the contrast easier to follow.

source.text: ἐὰν οὖν συνέλθῃ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὅλη ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πάντες λαλῶσιν γλώσσαις, εἰσέλθωσιν δὲ ἰδιῶται ἢ ἄπιστοι, οὐκ ἐροῦσιν ὅτι μαίνεσθε;

records.literal_gloss: If therefore comes together the church whole at the same [place] and all speak in tongues, come in but outsiders or unbelievers, not will they say that you are raving?

en.L: So if the whole church comes together in the same [place] and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, will they not say, "You are raving"?
en.B: Picture the whole church gathered in one place, with everyone speaking in tongues. If outsiders or unbelievers walk in, will they not say you have gone mad?
en.R: Imagine that the whole church meets together and everyone speaks in tongues. Then some people come in who do not understand, or who do not believe. They will say you have lost your minds!

fr.L: Si donc l’église tout entière se réunit au même [endroit] et que tous parlent en langues, et qu’entrent des non-initiés ou des incroyants, ne diront-ils pas : « Vous délirez » ?
fr.B: Imaginez toute l’église réunie en un même lieu, et tous parlant en langues. Si des non-initiés ou des incroyants entrent, ne diront-ils pas que vous avez perdu la raison ?
fr.R: Imaginez que toute l’église se réunit et que tout le monde parle en langues. Alors arrivent des gens qui ne comprennent pas, ou qui ne croient pas. Ils vont dire que vous êtes devenus fous !

decisions.choice: raving: out of one's mind, in a frenzy
decisions.reason: μαίνεσθε; means to be mad. Outsiders would hear something like the frenzy of some pagan cults (12:2), not the voice of God.

decisions.choice: outsiders or unbelievers: two groups, those who do not understand because they are new or lack the gift, and those who do not believe
alternatives: one group described in two ways
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, ἰδιῶται means a person who stands outside, here set beside ἄπιστοι. It may be someone interested in the faith but not yet a believer, or a believer who does not understand tongues; verse 24 has the same pair in the singular.

decisions.choice: the whole church in the same place: all the believers of the city meeting together
decisions.reason: Believers in Corinth usually met in houses (16:19). Romans 16:23, written from Corinth, calls Gaius host 'to the whole church'. Paul imagines all of them gathered and visitors coming in.

decisions.choice: will they not say?: they certainly will
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes.

decisions.choice: They will say you have lost your minds!
alternatives: Will they not say you are raving?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m4).

decisions.choice: people ... who do not understand
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Readable names the outsider by the one thing certain, that such a person does not understand.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ πάντες προφητεύωσιν, εἰσέλθῃ δέ τις ἄπιστος ἢ ἰδιώτης, ἐλέγχεται ὑπὸ πάντων, ἀνακρίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων, τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ φανερὰ γίνεται, καὶ οὕτως πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον προσκυνήσει τῷ θεῷ, ἀπαγγέλλων ὅτι Ὄντως ὁ θεὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: If but all prophesy, comes in but some unbeliever or outsider, he is convicted by all, he is examined by all, \v 25 the secrets of the heart of him manifest become, and thus having fallen on face he will worship the God, declaring that, Really the God among you is.

en.L: But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or outsider comes in, {{gender:they are|he is}} convicted by all, {{gender:they are|he is}} examined by all; \v 25 the secrets of {{gender:their|his}} heart become manifest, and so, falling on [the] face, {{gender:they|he}} will worship God, declaring, "Truly God is among you."
en.B: But if everyone is prophesying, and some unbeliever or outsider comes in, {{gender:they are|he is}} convicted by what all are saying and examined by what all are saying. \v 25 The secrets of {{gender:their|his}} heart come into the open, and so {{gender:they|he}} will fall face down and worship God, declaring, "God really is among you!"
en.R: But suppose everyone is prophesying when an unbeliever or someone who does not understand comes in. What everyone says will show {{gender:them|him}} {{gender:their|his}} sin and make {{gender:them|him}} look hard at {{gender:their|his}} life. \v 25 The secret things in {{gender:their|his}} heart will be brought out into the open. Then {{gender:they|he}} will bow down with {{gender:their|his}} face to the ground and worship God. {{gender:They|He}} will say, "God is truly here among you!"

fr.L: Mais si tous prophétisent, et qu’entre quelqu’un d’incroyant ou de non-initié, il est convaincu par tous, il est examiné par tous ; \v 25 les secrets de son cœur deviennent manifestes, et ainsi, tombant sur la face, il adorera Dieu, déclarant : « Vraiment, Dieu est parmi vous. »
fr.B: Mais si tous prophétisent et que survient quelqu’un d’incroyant ou de non-initié, il est convaincu par ce que tous disent et examiné par ce que tous disent. \v 25 Les secrets de son cœur sont mis au jour ; alors il se prosternera, face contre terre, pour adorer Dieu, et il déclarera : « Dieu est vraiment parmi vous ! »
fr.R: Mais imaginez que tout le monde prophétise quand arrive quelqu’un qui ne croit pas ou qui ne comprend pas. Ce que tous disent lui montrera son péché et l’obligera à examiner sérieusement sa vie. \v 25 Ce qui est caché dans son cœur sera mis en pleine lumière. Alors il s’inclinera, le visage contre terre, et il adorera Dieu. Il dira : « Dieu est vraiment ici, au milieu de vous ! »

decisions.choice: convicted: shown to be in the wrong, brought to see one's sin
decisions.reason: ἐλέγχεται means to expose, to prove someone guilty, and so to bring them to conviction (John 16:8; Ephesians 5:13).

decisions.choice: examined: searched and assessed
decisions.reason: ἀνακρίνεται is the verb for examining or judging in 2:14-15 and 4:3-4. What the prophets say probes the hearer's life.

decisions.choice: the secrets of the heart become manifest: God shows the hearer what lies hidden within
decisions.reason: Only God knows the secrets of the heart (4:5; Psalm 44:22). When prophecy lays them bare, the hearer knows that God is present. The stress is on what the hearer comes to see, not on prophets telling others' secrets.

decisions.choice: falling on the face: bowing to the ground, the posture of worship
decisions.reason: To fall on one's face was to bow fully to the ground before God or a king (Genesis 17:3; Matthew 2:11, where the Magi fall down and worship).

decisions.choice: God is really among you: words like Isaiah 45:14 and Zechariah 8:23
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 45:14 foreigners come and bow down to Israel, saying 'Surely God is among you'; in Zechariah 8:23 people of the nations say 'God is with you'. The outsider's confession fulfills what the prophets expected of the nations.

decisions.choice: among you: present in your gathering
alternatives: in you, within each of you
decisions.reason: ἐν ὑμῖν can mean 'among you' or 'in you'. The outsider speaks of what is seen in the gathered church.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}} and the related pronouns
decisions.reason: The person may be a man or a woman, so the gender setting applies; the Greek uses masculine forms for any person.

decisions.choice: show them their sin; make them look hard at their life
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words what being convicted and examined mean (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "quelqu’un d’incroyant ou de non-initié ... il ... son cœur", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs the gender setting on its pronouns. French follows the Greek "someone" with "quelqu’un", which already means a man or a woman, and the "il" and "son" that refer back to it are ordinary generic French (style guide 7); the same holds in 14:28 and 14:37-38.

source.text: Τί οὖν ἐστιν, ἀδελφοί;

records.literal_gloss: What then is it, brothers?

en.L: What then is [it], {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}?
en.B: What follows, then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}?
en.R: So what does all this mean for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}?

fr.L: Qu’en est-il donc, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} ?
fr.B: Que conclure, alors, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} ?
fr.R: Alors, qu’est-ce que tout cela veut dire pour vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} ?

decisions.choice: what then is it?: what follows?
decisions.reason: As in verse 15, the question leads to Paul's practical conclusion for their gatherings.

decisions.choice: What follows, then? (B); what does all this mean for you? (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 15, Balanced and Readable give the sense of the question.

source.text: ὅταν συνέρχησθε, ἕκαστος ψαλμὸν ἔχει, διδαχὴν ἔχει, ἀποκάλυψιν ἔχει, γλῶσσαν ἔχει, ἑρμηνείαν ἔχει· πάντα πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν γινέσθω.

records.literal_gloss: Whenever you come together, each a psalm has, a teaching has, a revelation has, a tongue has, an interpretation has; all things for building up let be done.

en.L: Whenever you come together, each one has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation; let all things be done for building up.
en.B: Whenever you gather, each of you has something: a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, an interpretation. Everything should be done to build up the church.
en.R: When you meet together, each of you has something to share. One person has a song of praise. Another has a teaching, or a revelation from God. Another speaks in a tongue, and another interprets it. Everything you do must help the church grow stronger.

fr.L: Quand vous vous réunissez, chacun a un psaume, a un enseignement, a une révélation, a une langue, a une interprétation ; que tout se fasse pour l’édification.
fr.B: Quand vous vous réunissez, chacun de vous a quelque chose : un psaume, un enseignement, une révélation, une langue, une interprétation. Que tout se fasse pour édifier l’église.
fr.R: Quand vous vous réunissez, chacun de vous a quelque chose à partager. L’un a un chant de louange. Un autre a un enseignement, ou une révélation de Dieu. Un autre parle en langue, et un autre interprète ce qu’il dit. Tout ce que vous faites doit aider l’église à devenir plus forte.

decisions.choice: each has: each person brings something, one this and another that
alternatives: every person has every one of these
decisions.reason: ἕκαστος with the repeated verb describes what happens when they meet: one has a psalm, another a teaching, and so on. Paul does not say that every believer has all five.

decisions.choice: a description of their gatherings, which Paul accepts and then regulates
alternatives: a mild rebuke: everyone wants a turn at once
decisions.reason: The sentence describes what each brings without blame, and the command that follows sets the rule for it. Some hear a complaint that everyone brings something and all want to speak, which verses 27-33 then put in order.

decisions.choice: psalm: a song of praise to God, perhaps a psalm of Scripture or a new song
decisions.reason: ψαλμὸν can be a psalm from the Old Testament or a song composed in the same manner (verse 15; Ephesians 5:19; Colossians 3:16).

decisions.choice: teaching, revelation, tongue, interpretation: the kinds of speech named in verse 6 and the gifts of 12:10
decisions.reason: ἀποκάλυψιν is a revelation given by God to a prophet (verse 30); γλῶσσαν and ἑρμηνείαν are a tongue and its interpretation.

decisions.choice: let all things be done for building up: the rule for every contribution
decisions.reason: The test of verses 3-5, 12 and 17 now governs everything done when the church meets.

decisions.choice: a song of praise
decisions.reason: Readable says what a psalm is (m3).

decisions.choice: the church
decisions.reason: The Greek says only 'for building up'; the church is what is built up, as in verses 4, 5 and 12.

source.text: εἴτε γλώσσῃ τις λαλεῖ, κατὰ δύο ἢ τὸ πλεῖστον τρεῖς, καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος, καὶ εἷς διερμηνευέτω·

records.literal_gloss: Whether in a tongue anyone speaks, by two or the most three, and in turn, and one let interpret;

en.L: If anyone speaks in a tongue, [let it be] by two, or at the most three, and in turn; and one is to interpret.
en.B: As for speaking in a tongue, let it be done by two people, or by three at the most, each taking a turn, and let one person interpret.
en.R: If people speak in tongues, only two or three should do it at a meeting. They should take turns, and one person must interpret what they say.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un parle en langue, [que ce soit] deux, ou tout au plus trois, et chacun à son tour ; et qu’un seul interprète.
fr.B: Quant à parler en langue, que cela se fasse par deux personnes, ou trois au plus, chacune à son tour, et qu’une seule personne interprète.
fr.R: Si des gens parlent en langues, seulement deux ou trois doivent le faire pendant une réunion. Ils doivent parler chacun à son tour, et une personne doit interpréter ce qu’ils disent.

decisions.choice: two or at the most three: at each gathering
alternatives: two or three at a time
decisions.reason: κατὰ δύο distributes: two, or three, on each occasion. The next words, 'in turn', rule out speaking at the same time.

decisions.choice: in turn: one after another
decisions.reason: ἀνὰ μέρος means by turns, each in their part.

decisions.choice: one: one person interprets, perhaps the same person for all who speak
decisions.reason: εἷς is the number one. It may simply mean 'someone', or that one person should interpret, so that interpreters do not compete. Verses 5 and 13 show that the speaker may also be the interpreter.

decisions.choice: [let it be] (L); at a meeting (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb for the numbers; Literal supplies one, and Readable says that the limit is for each gathering (m1).

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ διερμηνευτής, σιγάτω ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἑαυτῷ δὲ λαλείτω καὶ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: If but not there is an interpreter, let him be silent in church, to himself and let him speak and to the God.

en.L: But if there is no interpreter, let {{gender:them|him}} be silent in church, and let {{gender:them|him}} speak to {{gender:themselves|himself}} and to God.
en.B: If there is no one to interpret, the speaker should keep silent in the church, speaking only to {{gender:themselves|himself}} and to God.
en.R: If no one is there who can interpret, those who speak in tongues should be silent during the meeting. They can speak quietly to themselves and to God.

fr.L: Mais s’il n’y a pas d’interprète, qu’il se taise dans l’église, et qu’il parle à lui-même et à Dieu.
fr.B: S’il n’y a personne pour interpréter, celui qui parle doit se taire dans l’église, et ne parler qu’à lui-même et à Dieu.
fr.R: S’il n’y a personne qui puisse interpréter, ceux qui parlent en langues doivent se taire pendant la réunion. Ils peuvent parler tout bas, pour eux-mêmes et pour Dieu.

decisions.choice: be silent: stop speaking aloud in the gathering, in the situation described
decisions.reason: σιγάτω means to be or become silent. Paul uses the same verb for the speaker in tongues here, for a prophet in verse 30, and for women in verse 34. Here the silence applies only when no interpreter is present.

decisions.choice: speak to oneself and to God: pray in the tongue quietly, without addressing the church
alternatives: pray in tongues elsewhere, in private
decisions.reason: ἑαυτῷ ('to himself') sets this speech against speech to the church. Paul does not say whether it is quiet prayer during the meeting or prayer elsewhere; either way it is speech to God, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: an interpreter: someone with the gift of interpretation, who may be the speaker (verse 13)
decisions.reason: διερμηνευτής is the one who interprets, a gift named in 12:10.

decisions.choice: be silent (L, R); keep silent (B)
decisions.reason: The same English for the same verb in verses 28, 30 and 34, so that readers can compare them (m1).

decisions.choice: quietly
decisions.reason: Readable follows m2: the speaking is not addressed to the gathering.

decisions.choice: se taire at every level, in 14:28, 14:30 and 14:34
decisions.reason: The English keeps the same words for the same verb in the three verses so that readers can compare them (m1); French does the same with one verb at every level.

source.text: προφῆται δὲ δύο ἢ τρεῖς λαλείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι διακρινέτωσαν·

records.literal_gloss: Prophets and two or three let speak, and the others let weigh;

en.L: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh [what is said].
en.B: As for prophets, let two or three speak, and let the others weigh their words.
en.R: Two or three prophets may speak at a meeting. The others should think carefully about what they say, to see whether it comes from God.

fr.L: Et que deux ou trois prophètes parlent, et que les autres évaluent [ce qui est dit].
fr.B: Quant aux prophètes, que deux ou trois parlent, et que les autres évaluent leurs paroles.
fr.R: Deux ou trois prophètes peuvent parler pendant une réunion. Les autres doivent réfléchir avec soin à ce qu’ils disent, pour voir si cela vient de Dieu.

decisions.choice: weigh: assess what is said, to tell what comes from God
decisions.reason: διακρινέτωσαν is related to the gift of 'distinguishing of spirits' (12:10): telling apart what is from God's Spirit and what is not. Prophecy was to be tested, not simply accepted (1 Thessalonians 5:20-21; 1 John 4:1).

decisions.choice: the others: the other prophets present
decisions.reason: οἱ ἄλλοι most naturally means the rest of the group just named, the prophets. But testing prophecy is elsewhere the work of the whole church (1 Thessalonians 5:20-21), and all believers have the Spirit (12:3, 13), so some take it of everyone present.

decisions.choice: weigh
decisions.reason: 'Weigh' means to assess, not to condemn (m1).

decisions.choice: [what is said] (L); to see whether it comes from God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object; Readable says what weighing is for (m1).

decisions.choice: évaluer
decisions.reason: "Juger" can suggest condemning, which is not the sense (m1); "examiner" is kept for the other verb of 14:24. "Évaluer" says to weigh what is said, as the English "weigh" does.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ, ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω.

records.literal_gloss: If but to another it is revealed sitting, the first let be silent.

en.L: But if [something] is revealed to another who is sitting [there], let the first be silent.
en.B: And if something is revealed to another person who is sitting there, the first speaker should keep silent.
en.R: If God shows something to another person who is sitting there, the first prophet should be silent and let that person speak.

fr.L: Mais si [quelque chose] est révélé à un autre qui est assis [là], que le premier se taise.
fr.B: Et si quelque chose est révélé à un autre qui est assis là, le premier doit se taire.
fr.R: Si Dieu montre quelque chose à une autre personne assise là, le premier prophète doit se taire et la laisser parler.

decisions.choice: is revealed: God gives a revelation
decisions.reason: ἀποκαλυφθῇ is passive, with God as the one who reveals (2:10). This is the 'revelation' of verses 6 and 26, given to a prophet.

decisions.choice: sitting: the hearers sat while the one speaking stood
decisions.reason: A speaker could stand to address a gathering (Acts 13:16); here the others are seated. The word marks the person as one of the hearers.

decisions.choice: be silent: the first prophet stops, to let the other speak
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verses 28 and 34. Here it means giving way, as verse 31 explains: all can prophesy in turn.

decisions.choice: God shows; and let that person speak
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who reveals (m1) and says why the first prophet is silent (m3).

decisions.choice: be silent (L, R); keep silent (B)
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

source.text: δύνασθε γὰρ καθ’ ἕνα πάντες προφητεύειν, ἵνα πάντες μανθάνωσιν καὶ πάντες παρακαλῶνται καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ θεὸς ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης, ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων.

records.literal_gloss: You are able for one by one all to prophesy, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged \v 32 and spirits of prophets to prophets are subject, \v 33 not for is of disorder the God but of peace, as in all the churches of the holy ones.

en.L: For you are all able to prophesy one at a time, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged; \v 32 and prophets' spirits are subject to prophets, \v 33 for God is [the God] not of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the holy ones.
en.B: You can all prophesy, each in turn, so that all of you learn and all of you are encouraged. \v 32 Prophets have their own spirits under their control. \v 33 God is the God of peace, not of disorder, as is true in all the churches of God's holy people.
en.R: All of you can prophesy, one at a time, so that everyone can learn and everyone can be encouraged. \v 32 Prophets can control themselves when they prophesy. \v 33 God does not cause confusion. He brings peace. That is true in all the churches of God's people.

fr.L: Car vous pouvez tous prophétiser un par un, afin que tous apprennent et que tous soient encouragés ; \v 32 et les esprits des prophètes sont soumis aux prophètes, \v 33 car Dieu n’est pas [un Dieu] de désordre, mais de paix, comme dans toutes les églises des saints.
fr.B: Vous pouvez tous prophétiser, chacun à son tour, pour que tous apprennent et que tous soient encouragés. \v 32 Les prophètes gardent la maîtrise de leur propre esprit. \v 33 Dieu est un Dieu de paix, non de désordre ; il en est ainsi dans toutes les églises du peuple saint de Dieu.
fr.R: Vous pouvez tous prophétiser, l’un après l’autre, pour que tout le monde apprenne et que tout le monde soit encouragé. \v 32 Les prophètes peuvent se contrôler quand ils prophétisent. \v 33 Dieu ne provoque pas le désordre. Il apporte la paix. C’est ainsi dans toutes les églises du peuple de Dieu.

decisions.choice: you can all prophesy one by one: there is room for every prophet to speak, in turn
decisions.reason: ἕνα with the preposition before it means one at a time. πάντες probably means all who have the gift of prophecy, not every believer (12:29: not all are prophets).

decisions.choice: be encouraged: be urged on and strengthened
decisions.reason: παρακαλῶνται is the verb related to 'encouragement' in verse 3.

decisions.choice: the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets: prophets can control their own inspired speech, and so can wait their turn
alternatives: what one prophet says is subject to the assessment of the other prophets (verse 29)
decisions.reason: πνεύματα προφητῶν are the prophets' own spirits as God's Spirit moves them, as with 'my spirit' in verse 14. Prophecy does not seize a person against their will, so a prophet can stop to let another speak (verse 30). Others read the words with verse 29: what one prophet says is subject to the others who weigh it.

decisions.choice: God is not a God of disorder but of peace: the way the church meets should reflect who God is
